title: Toon Skit shot props (props.shot of every ext_toon_skit scene)
description: One cut of a cartoon skit: a set, a framing, up to three characters, and who is talking when.

sceneStart.description: Copy of this scene entry's startFrame (video frames). The speaker's mouth moves on the video's word timings, so it must match the scene's startFrame exactly.

set.description: Where the skit happens. Keep one set for a run of shots in the same place; change it only when the story moves.

framing.description: wide = everyone full length (establishing shots, entrances, the setup); two_shot = two characters, closer than the wide, still full length; close = one character (focus) head and chest, for a line that lands, a reaction or a punchline; back = one character (focus) seen from behind walking away (the exit, the ending).

focus.description: The id of the one character a close or back shot shows. Required for close and back; ignored otherwise.

cast.description: Characters in this shot. A close or back shot draws only the focus; a two_shot holds at most 2.

id.description: The character's id for the whole video: a, b or c. Use the same id for the same character in every scene.

look.description: What the character looks like. Give each character ONE look and copy it unchanged into every scene they appear in, or they read as a different person.

hair.description: Hair style. none = bald; balding = tufts over the ears only.

outfit.description: Costume: uniform (shirt with pockets, badge and belt: guard, officer, pilot), jumpsuit (one piece with a blank name patch: inmate, mechanic), suit (jacket, shirt, tie), hoodie, tshirt, lab_coat (white coat: doctor, scientist), apron (cook, shopkeeper), dress.

outfitColor.description: The costume's main colour (a lab coat stays white and this colours the shirt under it). Pick colours that differ between characters and pop against the muted set: orange, red, mustard, green, blue, purple.

hat.description: Hat: peaked_cap (an officer's cap), cap (a baseball cap), beanie, hard_hat (always yellow).

hatColor.description: The hat's colour; absent means the outfit colour.

slot.description: Where they stand in a wide or two-shot: left, center or right. Keep a character on the same side across shots (screen direction).

facing.description: Which way they face: toward the person they talk to (left of the pair faces right, right faces left). front = to camera. In a close-up, facing right puts them left of centre with room for a pointing arm.

poses.description: Body poses over the scene; each switches on its frame with no tween. point = arm straight out at the other; shrug = both palms up; hand_head = hand behind the head (embarrassed, thinking); finger_up = 'one thing...'; gesture = forearm out, bouncing as they talk; sit and sit_relaxed (leaning back, hand behind head) put them on the set's seat (cot, office chair, sofa, bench). At most 6 entries; a cut usually needs 1 or 2.

at.description: Frame of this scene (0 = the scene's first frame) from which it holds. The first entry is at 0.

pose.description: The pose from this frame on.

faces.description: Expressions over the scene; each switches on its frame. Change the face on the word that earns it (the reveal, the insult, the punchline). At most 6 entries.

at.description: Frame of this scene (0 = the scene's first frame) from which it holds. The first entry is at 0.

face.description: The face from this frame on.

talk.description: Who has the line from which frame of the scene: the speaker's mouth moves while words are spoken. 'none' for a pause, a sound or a reaction with nobody talking. First entry at 0; at most 8.

at.description: Frame of this scene from which this speaker holds.

who.description: The speaking character's id, or none.

push.description: A very slow 4% push in over the shot. Off by default (the style's camera is locked); use it on at most one or two tense shots per video.
